title: Postgres
description: The CloudNativePG cluster `postgres`: health, connections, load, I/O, WAL, replication, the pgbouncer pooler. Write-side panels read the primary (found by metric, not by pod name). Provisioned from git (kube-cluster/apps/grafana/dashboards/postgres); README there has the runbook.

links.title: Postgres databases
links.tooltip: Per-app view of one or more databases

panels.title: Primary
panels.description: The instance not in recovery. Red when there is not exactly one: a failover is in progress or the metrics stopped. Found by `cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery`, not the pod's role label, which the scrape drops.

panels.title: Instances up
panels.description: Instance exporters scraped successfully (of 3). At 2, one more loss pauses all writes (synchronous replication with `dataDurability: required`).

panels.title: Sync standbys
panels.description: Synchronous standbys the primary sees (`synchronous.number` is 1). At 0 every commit waits: writes pause until a standby is back.

panels.title: Replay lag (worst standby)
panels.description: How far the slowest standby's replay is behind, as the primary sees it. Reads on `postgres-ro` are this stale.

panels.title: Connections used
panels.description: Backends on the primary against `max_connections` (500). Near the ceiling, new connections fail: find the database in *Backends by database*.

panels.title: Longest idle in transaction
panels.description: Oldest transaction left open by an idle client, any database. It holds locks and stops vacuum from removing dead rows. Find it in *Transaction age by database*.

panels.title: Commits per second
panels.description: Committed transactions per second on the primary, all databases.

panels.title: WAL waiting to archive
panels.description: WAL segments on the primary marked ready but not yet archived. Rising means archiving to S3 is stuck and `pg_wal` will fill the disk: check the barman-cloud sidecar log, RGW and the `serverName` (infra/postgres/README.md).

panels.title: Last WAL archived
panels.description: Time since the primary last archived a WAL segment. `archive_timeout` is 5 min, so older means archiving fails or stalls.

panels.title: Last successful backup
panels.description: Age of the newest base backup in the object store, reported by the barman-cloud plugin. Backups run daily at 02:00.

panels.title: Last failed backup
panels.description: Time since the last failed backup. Red for a day after a failure: `kubectl -n postgres get backup` and describe the failed one.

panels.title: pgdata time to full
panels.description: Soonest an instance's data volume (data and WAL) fills, from the 6h trend. Grow `storage.size` in cluster.yaml (online); never delete a PV.

targets.expr: min((max by ("k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name") ({__name__="k8s.volume.available", k8s.namespace.name="postgres", k8s.volume.name="pgdata"}) / -deriv(max by ("k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name") ({__name__="k8s.volume.available", k8s.namespace.name="postgres", k8s.volume.name="pgdata"})[6h:5m]) and deriv(max by ("k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name") ({__name__="k8s.volume.available", k8s.namespace.name="postgres", k8s.volume.name="pgdata"})[6h:5m]) < 0)) or vector(1e10)

panels.title: Backends by state
panels.description: Client backends on the selected instances, by state. *idle in transaction* holds locks; a growing *idle* count is usually an app's connection pool sized too large.

panels.title: Backends by database
panels.description: The 15 databases with the most backends. A database near its app's pool size is the first suspect when *Connections used* climbs.

panels.title: Backends by role
panels.description: Backends by login role (the 15 largest). An app connecting with an unexpected role shows up here.

panels.title: Transaction age by database
panels.description: Oldest open transaction per database: *active* and *idle in transaction*. Idle in transaction past a minute is an app bug (missing commit, held across I/O); it blocks vacuum and DDL.

targets.expr: topk_max(10, max by (datname) (cnpg_backends_max_tx_duration_seconds{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", state=~"idle in transaction.*"}) > 0)

panels.title: Longest running statement
panels.description: Runtime of the longest active statement per database (10 largest). Long here and in *Lock waits* together means one statement blocks the others.

panels.title: Lock waits
panels.description: Backends waiting for a lock, per database, and the operator's cluster-wide count of backends blocked by another backend. Sustained waits: find the blocker with `pg_blocking_pids()` in psql.

panels.title: New sessions by database
panels.description: Connections opened per second (10 busiest). Each one forks a backend process; hundreds per minute from one app means it does not pool connections.

panels.title: Sessions ended abnormally
panels.description: Sessions per second that ended because the client vanished (*abandoned*), on a fatal error, or were terminated. Abandoned in bulk: an app or network dropping connections.

panels.title: Commits by database
panels.description: Committed transactions per second on the primary, 10 busiest databases.

panels.title: Rollbacks by database
panels.description: Rolled-back transactions per second on the primary. Some apps roll back on purpose; a jump in one database is an app erroring.

panels.title: Active backends by database
panels.description: Statement execution time per second, i.e. how many backends were busy on average: each database's share of the primary's work. The app at the top is the one to look at when the database is slow.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared_buffers, per instance and for the 5 lowest busy databases on the primary. Below ~0.95 the working set no longer fits: see *Memory* and *Cache pressure*. Misses may still hit the OS page cache.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_read{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

bottomk_min(5, sum by (datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{namespace="postgres", pod="$primary"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{namespace="postgres", pod="$primary"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_read{namespace="postgres", pod="$primary"}[$__rate_interval]))) and sum by (datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_read{namespace="postgres", pod="$primary"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{namespace="postgres", pod="$primary"}[$__rate_interval])) > 100)

panels.title: Time waiting on reads by database
panels.description: Seconds per second backends spent reading data blocks (needs `track_io_timing`). High with a low cache hit ratio: memory; high with a good one: slow storage (*I/O*).

panels.title: Mean block read latency
panels.description: Average time per block read from outside shared_buffers, per instance (needs `track_io_timing`). Under ~0.1 ms the OS cache served it; milliseconds mean the RBD volume.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blk_read_time{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_read{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Rows by operation
panels.description: Rows read (*returned* scanned, *fetched* by index) and written per second on the primary. Returned far above fetched means sequential scans: a missing index.

panels.title: Temp file bytes by database
panels.description: Bytes per second written to temp files by sorts and hashes that did not fit `work_mem` (4 MB). Sustained: that app needs an index or a larger `work_mem` for its role.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: Deadlocks detected per interval, by database. Each one aborted a transaction; repeated ones are an app taking locks in inconsistent order.

panels.title: Commit share by database
panels.description: Share of all commits on the primary, 8 busiest databases and the rest.

panels.title: Reads by process type
panels.description: Bytes per second read into shared_buffers by process type (pg_stat_io, relations). *client backend* is query traffic, *autovacuum* and *background worker* are maintenance.

panels.title: Writes by process type
panels.description: Bytes per second written out of shared_buffers. The *checkpointer* and *background writer* should do most of it; much from *client backend* means queries wait for buffers to be cleaned (shared_buffers or bgwriter too small).

panels.title: Relation I/O latency
panels.description: Mean time per read and per write of data blocks, per instance (needs `track_io_timing`).

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_io_read_time{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", object="relation"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_io_reads{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", object="relation"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_io_write_time{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", object="relation"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_io_writes{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", object="relation"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: WAL write and fsync latency
panels.description: Mean time per WAL write and per WAL fsync, per instance (needs `track_wal_io_timing`). Every commit waits for the primary's fsync and a standby's: this is the floor of commit latency.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_io_write_time{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", object="wal"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_io_writes{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", object="wal"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_io_fsync_time{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", object="wal"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_io_fsyncs{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$instance", object="wal"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Buffer evictions
panels.description: Buffers evicted per second to make room, by process type. High from client backends with a falling cache hit ratio: shared_buffers is too small for the working set.

panels.title: Node disk latency (RBD)
panels.description: Mean time per I/O on the RBD devices of the nodes running the selected instances. Node level: the other RBD volumes on that node share it, and no per-pod block I/O exists on k8s nodes.

targets.expr: sum by ("host.name") (rate({__name__="system.disk.operation_time", host.name=~"$server", device=~"rbd[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by ("host.name") (rate({__name__="system.disk.operations", host.name=~"$server", device=~"rbd[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Node disk throughput (RBD)
panels.description: Bytes per second on the RBD devices of the nodes running the selected instances, all volumes on the node.

panels.title: Node disk busy (RBD)
panels.description: Time per second the node's busiest RBD device had I/O in flight. Near 1 the device is saturated.

panels.title: Memory $instance
panels.description: Working set split into process memory (RSS), shared_buffers (shared memory, not in RSS, never reclaimed) and the active page cache, against the limit. The working set sits near the limit by design: the kernel keeps cache until it needs the room. Pressure shows as falling cache hit ratio and rising major faults, not here; RSS + shared_buffers near the limit is an OOM risk.

targets.expr: label_move(max by (pod) (cnpg_pg_settings_setting{namespace="postgres", pod="$instance", name="shared_buffers"}) * on (pod) max by (pod) (cnpg_pg_settings_setting{namespace="postgres", pod="$instance", name="block_size"}), "pod", "k8s.pod.name")

clamp_min(max by ("k8s.pod.name") ({__name__="container.memory.working_set", k8s.namespace.name="postgres", k8s.container.name="postgres", k8s.pod.name="$instance"}) - max by ("k8s.pod.name") ({__name__="container.memory.rss", k8s.namespace.name="postgres", k8s.container.name="postgres", k8s.pod.name="$instance"}) - label_move(max by (pod) (cnpg_pg_settings_setting{namespace="postgres", pod="$instance", name="shared_buffers"}) * on (pod) max by (pod) (cnpg_pg_settings_setting{namespace="postgres", pod="$instance", name="block_size"}), "pod", "k8s.pod.name"), 0)

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cores used by the postgres container, per instance. No CPU limit; the request is 250m.

panels.title: Cache pressure: major page faults
panels.description: Page faults per second that had to read from disk. Rising together with blocks read and a falling cache hit ratio: the page cache is squeezed; raise the memory limit (restarts the instances, batch it).

panels.title: Blocks read from outside shared_buffers
panels.description: Data blocks per second Postgres requested from the OS (page cache or disk), per instance.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Pod traffic per instance and direction. Transmit on the primary includes WAL streamed to both standbys and archived to S3.

panels.title: pgdata used
panels.description: Share of each instance's 20 Gi volume in use (data and WAL). Grow `storage.size` in cluster.yaml (online, grow only).

targets.expr: label_move(1 - max by ("k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name") ({__name__="k8s.volume.available", k8s.namespace.name="postgres", k8s.volume.name="pgdata"}) / max by ("k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name") ({__name__="k8s.volume.capacity", k8s.namespace.name="postgres", k8s.volume.name="pgdata"}), "k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name", "pvc")

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Size on disk of the 10 largest databases (primary).

panels.title: Database growth per day
panels.description: Size change per day from the trend over the last day, 10 fastest growing. Negative after a vacuum full or a cleanup.

panels.title: pg_wal
panels.description: WAL segments (16 MB) kept on the primary, against the checkpoint targets *min* and *max* (`min_wal_size`, `max_wal_size`). Far above *max*: archiving or a replication slot holds WAL.

panels.title: Transaction ID age
panels.description: Age of the oldest unfrozen transaction ID per database (5 oldest). Autovacuum freezes at 200M; near 2B Postgres stops accepting writes. Climbing past 200M: a long transaction or a slot blocks vacuum.

panels.title: WAL generated
panels.description: WAL bytes written per second on the primary; this is what replication and archiving have to carry.

panels.title: Full-page images
panels.description: Share of WAL records that are full-page images: high right after each checkpoint; constantly high means checkpoints are too frequent and inflate the WAL.

panels.title: WAL buffers full
panels.description: Times per interval a backend had to write WAL itself because the WAL buffers were full. Sustained non-zero: raise `wal_buffers`.

panels.title: Checkpoints
panels.description: Checkpoints per interval on the primary. *requested* (WAL reached `max_wal_size`) above *timed* (every 5 min) means `max_wal_size` (1 GB) is too small for the write rate.

panels.title: Checkpoint write and sync time
panels.description: Seconds per second the checkpointer spent writing and fsyncing data files. Sync time that grows means storage struggles with the flush.

panels.title: Background writer
panels.description: Buffers per second written by checkpoints and the background writer, and allocated. *maxwritten_clean* above zero: the bgwriter hit its per-round limit.

panels.title: WAL archiving
panels.description: Segments archived and failed per interval on the primary. Any failure: read the barman-cloud sidecar log.

panels.title: WAL archive backlog
panels.description: WAL segments on the primary waiting to be archived. Should stay near 0.

panels.title: Standby lag
panels.description: Write, flush and replay lag of each standby as the primary sees it. Write and flush lag add to commit latency (synchronous replication); replay lag is how stale `postgres-ro` reads are.

panels.title: Standby bytes behind
panels.description: WAL bytes each standby still has to replay, and WAL retained by each replication slot. A slot growing without bound pins WAL on the primary's disk.

panels.title: Standby replay delay
panels.description: Each standby's own view: seconds since the last replayed transaction while WAL is pending. 0 when caught up.

panels.title: Standby health
panels.description: 1 = a standby without a running WAL receiver: it is not streaming and falls behind. *streaming* is the number of standbys connected to the primary (should be 2).

panels.title: Instance restarts and role changes
panels.description: Postgres restarts and primary/standby flips per instance over time. A flip moves the primary: check Synapse afterwards (sequence guard, apps/matrix/README.md).

panels.title: Standby query conflicts
panels.description: Queries on standbys cancelled because replay needed to remove rows they could still see. Only matters for apps reading from `postgres-ro`.

panels.title: Pooler clients
panels.description: Client connections per pool (database/user) on the pgbouncer pods, active and waiting for a server connection. Empty while no app connects through `postgres-pooler`.

panels.title: Pooler server connections
panels.description: Server connections per pool: *active* paired with a client, *idle* ready, *used* recently released. A pool pinned at `default_pool_size` (25 per pod) with waiting clients needs a larger pool, not a larger database.

panels.title: Pooler max wait
panels.description: Longest time a client has been waiting for a server connection, per pool.

targets.expr: max by (database, user) (cnpg_pgbouncer_pools_maxwait{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$pooler", database!="pgbouncer"} + cnpg_pgbouncer_pools_maxwait_us{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$pooler", database!="pgbouncer"} / 1e6)

panels.title: Pooler queries
panels.description: Queries and transactions per second through the pooler, per database.

panels.title: Pooler query time
panels.description: Mean query time and mean client wait per query, per database, as pgbouncer measures them: the latency the app sees, minus its own network.

targets.expr: sum by (database) (rate(cnpg_pgbouncer_stats_total_query_time{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$pooler", database!="pgbouncer"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (database) (rate(cnpg_pgbouncer_stats_total_query_count{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$pooler", database!="pgbouncer"}[$__rate_interval])) / 1e6

sum by (database) (rate(cnpg_pgbouncer_stats_total_wait_time{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$pooler", database!="pgbouncer"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (database) (rate(cnpg_pgbouncer_stats_total_query_count{namespace="postgres", pod=~"$pooler", database!="pgbouncer"}[$__rate_interval])) / 1e6

panels.title: Pooler CPU
panels.description: Cores used per pgbouncer pod. pgbouncer is single-threaded: 1.0 is saturated.

panels.title: Scrape targets up
panels.description: 1 per exporter the OTel cluster collector scraped successfully: 3 instances (:9187) and 2 pooler pods (:9127).

panels.title: Exporter collection time
panels.description: Time each exporter took to collect, by collector. The scrape interval is 60 s; a custom query that pushes this up is the suspect.

panels.title: Exporter errors
panels.description: 1 when the last collection on that pod failed (a custom query error, a lost connection).

panels.title: pg_stat_statements evictions
panels.description: Statement entries evicted per interval because `pg_stat_statements.max` (5000) was reached. Sustained evictions lose statistics and churn the top-queries series: raise the max (restarts the instances).

panels.title: Samples per scrape
panels.description: Series each exporter returns. Grows with databases, backends' application names and pools.
